title: fix(tts): accept the released Fish Audio Drama 3 model id
body:
## What Problem This Solves
OpenClaw rejects Fish Audio's released Drama 3 model id `drama-3` (`invalid Fish Audio model "drama-3"`), so users can only select `drama-3-preview`.

## User Impact
Users can set `tts.providers.fish-audio.model: "drama-3"` (or `talk.providers.fish-audio.modelId: "drama-3"`). `drama-3-preview` is still accepted, and `s2.1-pro` stays the default.

## Why This Change Was Made
Fish released Drama 3 on 2026-10-13. Fish's OpenAPI TTS `model` header enum now lists `drama-3` (https://docs.fish.audio/features/text-to-speech/drama-3). Fish serves an unknown model id as `s2.1-pro` without an error, so the exact id matters. This adds `drama-3` to the plugin's model list and points the docs and examples at it.

## Evidence
- `pnpm test:extension fish-audio-speech`: 13/13 pass. The new `drama-3` case fails with `invalid Fish Audio model "drama-3"` when the `tts.ts` change is reverted.
- `pnpm format:docs:check` and `oxfmt --check extensions/fish-audio-speech` are clean.
- Live check against Fish's API (outside OpenClaw): text with paired word tags (`<whisper>…</whisper>`, `<soft>…</soft>` and others) was synthesized with each model header and transcribed with Fish ASR, 3 runs each. With `drama-3`, no run spoke a tag word. With `s2.1-pro` or a misspelled id, every run read 3 tag words aloud.


## Real behavior proof

Run locally against the live Fish Audio API with OpenClaw's own capability CLI (`openclaw infer tts convert --local`),
built from this branch and from the merge base. Each run used a throwaway `OPENCLAW_HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` /
`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` (`openclaw config file` resolved inside the scratch dir) and `FISH_API_KEY` from the environment
only. No config file was written; the provider picked up the key through its env fallback and used the default voice.

**After (PR head `a479484e91`)**: `drama-3` is accepted and Fish Audio returns real audio.

```text
$ node openclaw.mjs infer tts convert --local --provider fish-audio --model fish-audio/drama-3 \
    --text "[sound relieved] We made it." --output $E/after-drama3.mp3 --json
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "tts.convert",
  "transport": "local",
  "provider": "fish-audio",
  "attempts": [
    { "provider": "fish-audio", "outcome": "success", "reasonCode": "success", "personaBinding": "none", "latencyMs": 387 }
  ],
  "outputs": [ { "path": "$E/after-drama3.mp3", "format": "mp3", "voiceCompatible": false } ]
}
exit=0
$ ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=format_name,duration,size -of default=nw=1 $E/after-drama3.mp3
format_name=mp3
duration=1.880750
size=30092
```

**Before (merge base `1bae5ffaed`, current `main`)**: the same command is rejected before any request is sent.

```text
$ node openclaw.mjs infer tts convert --local --provider fish-audio --model fish-audio/drama-3 \
    --text "[sound relieved] We made it." --output $E/before-drama3.mp3 --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "invalid Fish Audio model \"drama-3\"" }
}
exit=1
```

`openclaw infer tts providers --json` on the PR head also lists `drama-3` first in the Fish Audio model list.

Note: on both commits the local `tsdown` build exits non-zero on the existing `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` gate
(`src/infra/sqlite-file-generation-worker.ts`). The bundle is still emitted and the CLI runs from it. This PR does not
cause or touch that.

Not covered here: delivery through a real channel (for example a Telegram Test Server voice note). This is a CLI and
provider-level proof only.
